<[a specific online forum]>  
One of my favourite comedies.

To examine why Kurushima lost:  
Fucking Kurushima sucks ass as a Blue player. He could've just you know, left a few mana untapped to prepare his counters and his next Jester. There's no point in trying to push the advantage when you've got a clear upper hand in playing slow.  
The thing that surprises me the most is how much of an amateur he is at the game. While he had the thoughts of "He can't possibly ramp since that's really unlikely and he's playing Black" is alright, he decided to forego basic strategy and Leeroy-Jenkins'd his win into a loss. This kind of Blue deck, which wins by a combo and not through creatures, is pretty defensive by nature. How they stay alive until the combo is through a mix of counter and bounce cards. This is demonstrated to us when he simply conceded in the second game as he didn't counter the Megrim, and couldn't bounce it.  
As he wasn't playing any bounces, he should've had a counter card in hand with mana open. Two counters would've ensured him a win, even if he had to take it slow for a few turns as Hajime could only really play two spells a turn due to his land situation.

For the card-by-card analysis, a lot of the same was from last chapter, so let's go over the few "new" cards:

- [Megrim](https://gatherer.wizards.com/pages/card/Details.aspx?multiverseid=25631) - Enchantment - 2B:  
>Whenever an opponent discards a card, Megrim deals 2 damage to that player.

  I'll say, last chapter when I talked about strategies against his combo, I talked about targetting key pieces through artifact or land removal, but I completely forgot about one of Black's memest decks, *[Rack](https://www.channelfireball.com/all-strategy/articles/deck-of-the-day-modern-8-rack/)*. The modern version focuses less on discard triggers, but more on effects that happen when the opponent has no cards, even if the core identity of the deck is still the same.  
This card is pretty shit by modern-day standards, since the only deck I can think of that has you discarding a lot of cards is [Hollow One](https://gatherer.wizards.com/pages/Card/Details.aspx?multiverseid=430852), and if you're the one playing Megrim... Just play 8-rack instead? Though well, it *is* the perfect hard-counter to Mind Over Matter.

- [Jester's Cap](https://gatherer.wizards.com/Pages/Card/Details.aspx?multiverseid=3797) - Artifact - 4:  
>2, Tap, Sacrifice Jester's Cap: Search target player's library for three cards and exile them. Then that player shuffles their library.

  ngl this is also been power-creeped into hell. It's good, definitely so, as you can search for things in the library directly, without them having ever played it, but it only targets 3, doesn't search hand, and is bloody expensive. Look at [Surgical Extraction](https://gatherer.wizards.com/Pages/Card/Details.aspx?multiverseid=397706) or the Standard-legal [Unmoored Ego](https://gatherer.wizards.com/Pages/Card/Details.aspx?multiverseid=452962). Look at the costs, the speed at which you can use the effects. It's just you know, straight-up better?  
Brilliant hate card, too bad times have moved on.

- [Wasteland](https://gatherer.wizards.com/Pages/Card/Details.aspx?multiverseid=413790) - Land:  
> Tap: Add Colorless.  
Tap, Sacrifice Wasteland: Destroy target nonbasic land.

  I love the simplicity in this card. Too bad it's not in Modern, Pioneer, or Standard, and we're just left with [Field of Ruin](https://gatherer.wizards.com/pages/card/details.aspx?name=Field%20of%20Ruin) or any other variation of Wasteland. This is a very good 1-to-1 trade, since you're always bound to get the better end of the deal. It's nice to remove their key pieces, or to simply stifle them when you're ahead on mana.

- [Intuition](https://gatherer.wizards.com/Pages/Card/Details.aspx?multiverseid=397633) - Instant - 2U:  
>Search your library for three cards and reveal them. Target opponent chooses one. Put that card into your hand and the rest into your graveyard. Then shuffle your library.

  3 mana "I get this card" for Blue is pretty nasty. I'm glad that it's not in Modern to enable bullshit combos.  
Tutor effects are always hard to balance. Even letting the opponent choose, and putting the cards into the graveyard so you cannot draw them anymore aren't really downsides, since the graveyard is just another resource. I really don't want to see Grixis reanimator being a thing.

  > Sacrifice an enchantment: You gain life equal to the sacrificed enchantment's converted mana cost.

  > P/T: 1/1

  > *The power of faith is quiet. It is the leaf unmoved by the hurricane.*

  My first thought "This card is pretty shit. Shit or jank." And after looking around a bit, I don't think anyone really plays this apart from EDH enchantment/aura decks. There are certainly some good cards that go with this, like [Bruna](https://gatherer.wizards.com/Pages/Card/Details.aspx?multiverseid=240208) or [Hatching Plans](https://gatherer.wizards.com/Pages/Card/Details.aspx?name=Hatching%20Plans). So, I went digging through all 159 [enchantment cards in Urza block](https://scryfall.com/search?as=grid&order=name&q=type%3Aenchantment+block%3Ausg) to see why exactly this was made. - #####  [Arc Lightning](https://gatherer.wizards.com/Pages/Card/Details.aspx?multiverseid=5733) - Sorcery - 2R:

  > Arc Lightning deals 3 damage divided as you choose among one, two, or three targets.

  > *Rainclouds don't last long in Shiv, but that doesn't stop the lightning.*

  Yikes. This spell isn't that good, it has a low mana efficiency of 1 mana per damage, and it's not even instant speed. At least it's modal... To see why I'm complaining about this mana efficiency, see (1 damage) [Gut Shot](https://gatherer.wizards.com/Pages/Card/Details.aspx?multiverseid=397673), [Lava Dart](https://gatherer.wizards.com/Pages/Card/Details.aspx?multiverseid=464083), [Searing Blaze](https://gatherer.wizards.com/pages/card/Details.aspx?multiverseid=193982); (2 damage) [Shock](https://gatherer.wizards.com/Pages/Card/Details.aspx?multiverseid=466914), [Searing Blood](https://gatherer.wizards.com/Pages/Card/Details.aspx?multiverseid=378483); (3 damage) [Lightning Strike](https://gatherer.wizards.com/Pages/Card/Details.aspx?multiverseid=476108), [Lightning Bolt](https://gatherer.wizards.com/Pages/Card/Details.aspx?multiverseid=485315), [Lightning Helix](https://gatherer.wizards.com/Pages/Card/Details.aspx?multiverseid=455767).  
One of the most important things about burn spells is how much they cost. You want to be able to Lava Dart your opponent's Llanowar Elf on turn 1, not turn 3 when they have 12 mana floating from tron, ramp and dorks. 3 damage on turn 3 is simply too low and too *late*.  
Well, at least it's not the worst burn spell. I can see this being okay in draft, but...
